bar.name: v1 HTML fixtures and A2UI for the same apps; 300 blind English requests; independent end-to-end attack on stored rows

biggest_gap: restore(snapshot) of a backup that is ahead of the running program takes the backup's newest name map but keeps the older program, so names point at the wrong slots and new rows are stored swapped. Needs a stale second device or reinstall; not reachable inside one app.

acceptance.line: >= 90% of 300 blind requests expressible (programs parse and type-check)
acceptance.evidence: mo.mjs check passes 30 examples and 300 corpus programs; the GBNF accepts all 330. Coverage of unseen requests not re-measured.
300 corpus programs: keyword tokenizer median 133, p90 239, max 811.

acceptance.line: every prefix cut at a line end parses
acceptance.evidence: Prefix test passes inside 539/539; fuzz-check 20,000 mutations on a fresh seed: 0 crashes, 0 grammar disagreements.

acceptance.line: edits never lose or retype saved data while marked safe
acceptance.evidence: All round 5 faults fixed; critic's own slot-model fuzz (59k steps, 24 seeds, reload after every step) and 166 hand sequences find nothing inside one app. Open: newer backup into older program (S1), reused dropped-option name marked safe (S2), setting/state pick rename strands value (S2).

other_notes: S2: renaming an option onto the name of a dropped option is verdict safe and merges the two groups in counts and filters. S2: pick options of a top-level setting or state have no slots, so `Z was B` leaves the stored choice on B.

S3: load of a changed text that still has `was` acts as an edit; history that cannot express the snapshot wins silently; a typed '#Food' in a field widened from pick reads as the option; restore of another app's backup is accepted; missing version map gives a raw JS message.
Slot ids never leaked into trees, filters, charts, sort or forms. Six hand-computed programs match the evaluator.
